ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p322/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p322/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p322/r2.claim: Verses 16–19 shift to hypocrites as the Muslims’ hidden enemy: they hear the Prophet but understand nothing, and what strengthens believers’ faith strengthens their hypocrisy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p322/r2.anchor: These people do apparently listen to what the Prophet (sws) says but understand nothing.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r1.claim: The section on verses 16–38 continues the sūrah’s hypocrite theme; a major campaign makes it essential to expose hidden Muslims whose weakness and collusion threaten the community.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r1.anchor: When Muslims were asked to undertake a big campaign, it became essential that a group lurking among them as their hidden enemy be exposed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r2.claim: Islahi says the Qur’an discusses hypocrites in the same manner in al-Nisāʾ, al-Māʾidah, al-Anfāl, al-Tawbah, and other sūrahs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r2.anchor: They are mentioned here with the same reference as they are mentioned in S ūrah al-Nisā’, S ūrah al-Mā’idah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r3.claim: The first section depicts listeners who understand nothing and await punishment’s sign, unaware that a messenger’s advent already portends punishment for unbelievers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p335/r3.anchor: there is a group among the Muslims who does listen to what he says, yet understands nothing.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r1.claim: A hypocritical group attends the Prophet without seeking understanding, then asks the gathering's knowledgeable people what he said after they leave.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r1.anchor: when these people disperse from his presence, they ask from other knowledgeable people of the gathering what the Prophet (sws) had said

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r2.claim: Among those who reject revelation, one group avoids the Prophet out of aversion, while another comes only to feign listening; both are hypocritical.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r2.anchor: another one among them comes to him but not to listen and to understand; only to display its hypocrisy

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r3.claim: Their question about what he said lets them pretend they heard him and are ready to obey, while claiming they could not understand, thus concealing hypocrisy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r3.anchor: as far as hearing the Prophet (sws) is concerned, they have fully heard what he has said

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r4.claim: They insinuate that revelation needs deep deliberation and that believers accept the Prophet's words as simpletons; this tactic undermines the message, as their taunt about whose faith a sūrah revived illustrates.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p338/r4.anchor: by this comment they would insinuate agony for the Muslims who would believe and show conviction in everything related to them by the Prophet (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r2.claim: Those described in verse 16 are like the people in verse 14: their misdeeds have become attractive, so they follow base desires and face the same fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r2.anchor: their misdeeds have been endeared to them and they have become the followers of their base desires

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r3.claim: By their misdeeds, such people lose the innate light of vision and therefore remain deprived of revelation and have sealed hearts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p339/r3.anchor: Such people deprive themselves of the light of vision which the Almighty has innately blessed man with

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r19.claim: Ānifan and ānifan are active participles meaning “beginning”; their verb is unused, while iʾtanafa is used for beginning something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r19.anchor: آئفا وآنفا: هما اسما فاعل، ولم يستعمل فعلهما، والذي استعمل ائتنف، وهما بمعنى مبتديا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r20.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r20.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the expression from istanaftu al-shayʾ, “I began the thing”; interpreting it as “just now” conveys the sense rather than the literal wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p455/r20.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هو من استأنفت الشيء، إذا ابتدأته. فأولى لهم، قال صاحب الصحاح: قول العرب أولى لك: تهديد وتوعيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r13.claim: سقوا agrees with the semantic sense of من, while خالد agrees with its form; خرجوا likewise agrees with the meaning of من يستمع.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r13.anchor: وسقوا: عائد على معنى من، وهو خالد على اللفظ وكذا: خرجوا: على معنى من يستمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r14.claim: Hypocrites listened to the Prophet, then mockingly asked knowledgeable listeners what he had just said, pretending not to understand or see its benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467/r14.anchor: كان المنافقون يحضرون عند الرسول ويستمعون كلامه وتلاوته، فإذا خرجوا، قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud was among those whom the hypocrites asked what the Prophet had just said.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r2.claim: آنفا is a circumstantial expression meaning the statement he had just begun before the listener left.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r2.anchor: وآنفا: حال أي مبتدأ، أي: ما القول الذي ائتنفه قبل انفصاله عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r3.claim: The majority read آنفا on the pattern فاعل, while Ibn Kathir reads it on the pattern فعل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: آنفا، على وزن فاعل وابن كثير: على وزن فعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses آنفا as an adverb of time, based on its gloss as just now.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وآنفا نصب على الظرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the adverb parse: although exegetes gloss it as the recent past, no grammarian treats it as an adverb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p467#2/r5.anchor: والصحيح أنه ليس بظرف، ولا نعلم أحدا من النحاة عده في الظروف

STUDYQURAN:47:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:47:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:47:intro/r5.claim: The surah stresses diseased hearts, why God seals or locks them, and the intrinsic link between deeds, belief, and the heart’s state.
STUDYQURAN:47:intro/r5.anchor: The disease of hearts (vv. 20, 29) and the reasons for which God seals (v. 16) and locks (v. 24) them is an important theme of this sūrah

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r1.claim: The pronoun may refer broadly to people, as in the Quran's mention of some people after describing disbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r1.anchor: أن يكون الضمير عائدا إلى الناس

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to the people of Mecca, mentioned earlier as the community that expelled Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون راجعا إلى أهل مكة ، لأن ذكرهم سبق في قوله تعالى : { هي أشد قوة من قريتك التي

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r3.claim: A third reading makes them some of those described in the previous verse as destined for Hell and given boiling water.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون راجعا إلى معنى قوله { كمن هو خالد في النار وسقوا ماء حميما }

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r4.claim: The plural خرجوا follows the pronoun's plural sense, while singular يستمع follows its grammatical form.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r4.anchor: حمل على المعنى الذي هو الجمع ، ويستمع حمل على اللفظ

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r5.claim: Commentators treat حتى as a conjunction requiring the second clause to be part of, or a limit within, the first; unlike واو, it cannot join unrelated clauses.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r5.anchor: العطف بحتى لا يحسن إلا إذا كان المعطوف جزءا من المعطوف عليه إما أعلاه أو دونه ، كقول القائل

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r6.claim: The clause about their leaving adds that they listen intensely and ask the learned to repeat the Prophet's words, as a diligent student seeking understanding would.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r6.anchor: وجه التعلق ههنا هو أن قوله { حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك } يفيد معنى زائدا في الاستماع كأنه يقول : يستمعون استماعا بالغا جيدا

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r7.claim: One explanation is that they ask sarcastically, like a clever person telling a dull person to repeat himself while pretending to listen closely; others know he is mocking and not seeking instruction.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r7.anchor: إما كونهم بذلك مستهزئين ، كالذكي يقول للبليد : أعد كلامك حتى أفهمه

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r8.claim: Another explanation is that they fail to understand despite listening and asking for repetition, which fits the description of sealed hearts.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r8.anchor: وإما كونهم لا يفهمون مع أنهم يستمعون ويستعيدون ، ويناسب هذا الثاني قوله تعالى : { كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الكافرين }

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r9.claim: Some commentators say آنفا means just now, deriving it from isti'naf, the beginning of something.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r9.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين : معناه الساعة ، ومنه الاستئناف وهو الابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r10.claim: Al-Razi prefers “from the beginning”: they ask for the Prophet's words to be repeated from their start so they miss nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v28p50#2/r10.anchor: فعلى هذا فالأولى أن يقال يقولون ماذا قال آنفا بمعنى أنهم يستعيدون كلامه من الابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v28p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p51/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p51/r1.claim: They turned away from truth either because they could not understand or because they did not listen to benefit, and instead followed its opposite, their desires.
RAZI-FULL:v28p51/r1.anchor: أي تركوا اتباع الحق إما بسبب عدم الفهم ، أو بسبب عدم الاستماع للاستفادة واتبعوا ضده

STUDYQURAN:47:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r1.claim: “Among them” refers to Madinah’s hypocrites, while those given knowledge are the Prophet’s Companions.
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r1.anchor: Among them refers to the hypocrites of Madinah, while those who have been given knowledge refers to the Prophet’s Companions (Q, Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:47:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r2.claim: The sealed hearts hear the words and profess belief outwardly but are blinded by caprice, so they neither understand nor act on what they hear.
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r2.anchor: although they hear the words and profess belief outwardly, they are blinded by their desire to follow their caprices

STUDYQURAN:47:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r3.claim: Believers are also warned to attend to Quran recitation lest they hear without understanding or heeding it.
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r3.anchor: message to believers that they must be attentive when reciting the Quran, lest they hear the words but do not understand them or heed their meaning

STUDYQURAN:47:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r4.speaker: al-Ghazzālī
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r4.claim: Al-Ghazzālī lists four obstacles to understanding the Quran: focusing only on correct pronunciation; dogmatically adhering to a school; persistence in sin, pride, or worldly passions; and assuming the Quran contains only meanings transmitted by early commentators.
STUDYQURAN:47:16/r4.anchor: al-Ghazzālī lists four obstacles that prevent those who listen to the Quran from understanding it: confining their focus to the correct pronunciation

TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r1.claim: The listener is a hypocrite who hears the Prophet but fails to understand, treating the recitation and call to faith with contempt and heedlessness.
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك} [محمد: 16]

TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r2.claim: After leaving the Prophet, they ask the learned people who attended what Muhammad had just said, showing that they did not attend to his words.
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r2.anchor: قالوا إعلاما منهم لمن حضر معهم مجلسك من أهل العلم بكتاب الله، وتلاوتك عليهم ما تلوت، وقيلك لهم ما قلت

TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r3.claim: Qatadah describes hypocrites and three kinds of hearers: one who hears and acts, one inattentive hearer, and one who hears but abandons the message.
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك} [محمد: 16] " هؤلاء المنافقون، دخل رجلان

TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says he himself was among those whom people asked what the Prophet had just said.
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «أنا منهم، وقد سئلت فيمن سئل»

TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the listeners as hypocrites and the people endowed with knowledge as the Companions.
TAB-FULL:v21p203#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك}

BURSEVI:v8p393#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p393#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p393#3/r3.claim: People of the heart polish away blameworthy traits and witness signs of truth, gaining insight; people of the lower self beautify innovations and breaches of law, follow desires in belief and action, and stray from God and Paradise.
BURSEVI:v8p393#3/r3.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أهل القلب ، وأهل النفس ، فإن أهل القلب بسبب تصفية قلوبهم

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r1.claim: The hypocrites attended the Prophet’s assembly and heard his speech but, through disdain, neither comprehended it nor observed it properly.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r1.anchor: وهم المنافقون كانوا يحضرون مجلس رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ، فيسمعون كلامه ولا يعونه

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r2.claim: The plural خرجوا follows the semantic plurality of من, whereas the preceding singular follows its grammatical form.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r2.anchor: جمع الضمير باعتبار معنى من كما أن إفراده فيما قبله باعتبار لفظه

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r3.claim: The people endowed with knowledge are Companions learned in religion, including Abdullah ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and Abu al-Darda.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r3.anchor: يعني : علماء الصحابة كعبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه ، وابن عباس وأبي الدرداء رضي الله عنهم.

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r4.claim: Their question about what the Prophet just said is mockery disguised as a request for information: they pretend not to have understood.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r4.anchor: على طريق الاستهزاء ، وإن كان بصورة الاستعلام.

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r5.claim: آنفا derives metaphorically from the nose for something newly beginning or preceding the present.

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r6.claim: Al-Raghib explains استأنفت الشيء as taking its beginning, hence ماذا قال آنفا means what he began or said just now.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r6.anchor: قال الراغب : استأنفت الشيء أخذت آنفه ؛ أي : مبدأه. ومنه : ماذا قال آنفا ؛ أي : مبتدأ انتهى.

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r7.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r7.claim: Al-Qamus glosses آنفا as a little while ago or at the first nearby time, the hour immediately before the current one, resolving the objection that it means the present hour.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r7.anchor: وفي "القاموس" ، قال : آنفا كصاحب وكتف وقرىء بهما ؛ أي : مذ ساعة ؛ أي : في أول وقت يقرب منا.

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r8.claim: God sealed their hearts because they no longer turn toward good.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r8.anchor: ختم عليها لعدم توجهها نحو الخير أصلا

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r9.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r9.claim: Al-Raghib defines طبع as forming something in a particular shape, broader than sealing but narrower than engraving; the stamp is the instrument that imprints and seals.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r9.anchor: قال الراغب : الطبع أن يصور الشيء بصورة ما كطبع السكة وطبع الدراهم ، وهو أعم من الختم وأخص من النقش

BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r10.claim: Their false desires explain their fruitless conduct.
BURSEVI:v8p396#2/r10.anchor: فلذلك فعلوا ما فعلوا مما لا خير فيه.

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r1.claim: These verses continue the preceding discussion of diseased hearts, hypocrites, and those who apostatized after faith.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات جارية على السياق السابق

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r2.claim: Ānifan is an adverb for just before the present moment, or this very moment; it derives from anf, nose.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r2.anchor: آنفا اسم فاعل منصوب على الظرفية أو لكونه مفعولا فيه

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r3.claim: The pronoun refers to unbelievers; listening means attending to the Prophet's Quran recitation and exposition of religious principles and laws.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r3.anchor: والمراد باستماعهم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إصغاؤهم إلى ما يتلوه من القرآن

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r4.claim: The plural pronoun refers to the relative group by sense, while the earlier singular يستمع follows the relative's grammatical form.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r4.anchor: الضمير للموصول وجمع الضمير باعتبار المعنى كما أن إفراده

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r5.claim: Those given knowledge are companions who know God; the pronoun in their question refers to the Prophet.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r5.anchor: المراد بالذين أوتوا العلم العلماء بالله من الصحابة

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r6.claim: One reading takes the question as genuine inquiry: arrogance and desire kept them from understanding truth, as 4:78 also says.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r6.anchor: قيل للاستعلام حقيقة لأن استغراقهم في الكبر والغرور

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r7.claim: A second reported reading is mockery; al-Tabatabai considers this interpretation plausible.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r7.anchor: وقيل للاستهزاء، وقيل للتحقير كأن القول

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r8.claim: A third reading is contempt: they imply the speech is full of falsehoods and has no coherent meaning; the author says each reading has a basis.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r8.anchor: وقيل للتحقير كأن القول لكونه مشحونا بالأباطيل

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r9.claim: The first clause identifies them and the second restates it explanatorily; following desires signals a sealed heart, while one pure in original nature grasps divine truths readily.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r9.anchor: تعريف بعد تعريف فهو كعطف التفسير

TABATABAI:47:16-18/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r14.claim: By contrast, sealing signifies loss of perfected knowledge and following desires loss of righteous action; this does not conflict with reading the second clause as explanatory of the first.
TABATABAI:47:16-18/r14.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي ما قدمنا أن اتباع الأهواء كعطف التفسير

TABRISI:47:16/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
TABRISI:47:16/r1.claim: In some transmissions Ibn Kathīr reads the word short, anfan; the famous reading lengthens it, ānifan.
TABRISI:47:16/r1.anchor: روي في بعض الروايات عن ابن كثير أنفا بالقصر والقراءة المشهورة آنفا بالمد

TABRISI:47:16/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r2.speaker: أبو علي عن أبي زيد
TABRISI:47:16/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī cites Abū Zayd's poetry: al-anf describes noble people who disdain enduring humiliation; the other line uses muʾtanafan for a newly begun sacred month, with “month” omitted.
TABRISI:47:16/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي أنشد أبو زيد

TABRISI:47:16/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:47:16/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the poetic form al-anf is a plural pattern supported by another poet's al-anf al-nuṣūr.
TABRISI:47:16/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: فإذا كان كذلك فقد جمع فعل على فعل

TABRISI:47:16/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:47:16/r4.claim: The poetic examples concern disdain, not the verse's meaning of “just now”; no form anaf meaning beginning is attested. The short reading may analogize forms such as ḥādhir/ḥadhir, but the long reading derives from beginning.
TABRISI:47:16/r4.anchor: وليس الأنف والإنف في البيتين مما في الآية في شيء لأن ما في الشعر من الآنفة وما في الآية من الابتداء ولم يسمع أنف في معنى ابتداء

TABRISI:47:16/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r5.claim: Ānifan derives from iʾtināf, beginning, and means at a recent or just-past time.
TABRISI:47:16/r5.anchor: والوجه المد والآنف الجائي من الائتناف وهو الابتداء فقوله آنفا أي في أول وقت يقرب منا

TABRISI:47:16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r6.claim: Al-ahwāʾ is the plural of hawā, the soul's desire; istahwā means to call someone toward desire.
TABRISI:47:16/r6.anchor: الأهواء جمع الهوى وهو شهوة النفس يقال هوى يهوي هوى فهو هو واستهواه هذا الأمر أي دعاه إلى الهوى

TABRISI:47:16/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r10.claim: The listeners are among the previously mentioned disbelievers; a hypocrite is a disbeliever, and they hear the Prophet's recitation, call, and speech.
TABRISI:47:16/r10.anchor: ومن الكافرين الذين تقدم ذكرهم من يستمع إلى قراءتك ودعوتك وكلامك لأن المنافق كافر

TABRISI:47:16/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r11.claim: Those given knowledge are believers whom God gave knowledge and understanding.
TABRISI:47:16/r11.anchor: يعني الذين آتاهم الله العلم والفهم من المؤمنين

TABRISI:47:16/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:47:16/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he is among those given knowledge of the Qurʾān.
TABRISI:47:16/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنا ممن أوتوا العلم بالقرآن

TABRISI:47:16/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r13.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABRISI:47:16/r13.claim: ʿAlī says he and others who retained the Prophet's revelation would leave, whereupon the hypocrites asked what the Prophet had just said.
TABRISI:47:16/r13.anchor: وعن الأصبغ بن نباته عن علي ع قال: إنا كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيخبرنا بالوحي فأعيه أنا ومن يعيه

TABRISI:47:16/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r14.claim: One explanation is that they asked mockingly or pretended they had not attended to or understood the Prophet's words.
TABRISI:47:16/r14.anchor: وإنما قالوه استهزاء أو إظهار إنا لم نشتغل أيضا بوعيه وفهمه

TABRISI:47:16/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r15.claim: Another explanation is that they had not understood what they heard.
TABRISI:47:16/r15.anchor: وقيل: إنما قالوا ذلك لأنهم لم يفهموا معناه ولم يعلموا ما سمعوه

TABRISI:47:16/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r16.claim: A third view is that they belittled the Prophet's speech as containing nothing useful.
TABRISI:47:16/r16.anchor: وقيل: بل قالوا ذلك تحقيرا لقوله أي لم يقل شيئا فيه فائدة

TABRISI:47:16/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r17.claim: They may also have asked out of ostentatious hypocrisy, pretending they had forgotten only this and wanted it repeated so they could memorize it.
TABRISI:47:16/r17.anchor: ويحتمل أيضا أن يكونوا سألوا رياء ونفاقا أي لم يذهب عني من قوله إلا هذا فماذا قال أعده علي لأحفظه

TABRISI:47:16/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r18.claim: The shift from singular in “who listens” to plural in “when they leave” reflects the difference between min's singular form and plural meaning.
TABRISI:47:16/r18.anchor: لأن في الأول رد الضمير إلى لفظة من وفي الثاني إلى معناه فإنه موحد اللفظ مجموع المعنى

TABRISI:47:16/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r19.claim: The hearts were either marked with the stamp of disbelief or left to the people's own choice.
TABRISI:47:16/r19.anchor: أي وسم قلوبهم بسمة الكفار أو خلى بينهم وبين اختيارهم

TABRISI:47:16/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:47:16/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:47:16/r20.claim: They followed their desires and natural inclinations instead of what proof established.
TABRISI:47:16/r20.anchor: أي شهوات نفوسهم وما مالت إليه طباعهم دون ما قامت عليه الحجة

THALABI:v9p32#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p32#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p32#2/r7.claim: Those who listen are hypocrites who fail to comprehend or retain the Prophet's words out of disdain and pretended inattention.
THALABI:v9p32#2/r7.anchor: ومنهم يعني ومن هؤلاء الكفار من يستمع إليك وهم المنافقون يستمعون قولك، فلا يعونه، ولا يفهمونه تهاونا منهم بذلك، وتغافلا

THALABI:v9p32#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p32#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v9p32#2/r8.claim: Muqatil says that after the Prophet preached and admonished them, hypocrites left the mosque and mockingly asked Ibn Masud what he had just said.
THALABI:v9p32#2/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطب ويحث المنافقين، فسمع المنافقون قوله،

THALABI:v9p32#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p32#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p32#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says of those given knowledge: I am among them, and I was among those asked.
THALABI:v9p32#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله: قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم: أنا منهم وقد سئلت فيمن سئل.

THALABI:v9p32#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p32#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v9p32#2/r10.claim: Qatada identifies those whose hearts are sealed as the hypocrites.

THALABI:v9p32#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p32#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v9p32#2/r11.claim: Qatada distinguishes a man who understood and benefited from what he heard from one who did not; a maxim divides listeners into understanding, practicing, and heedless listeners.
THALABI:v9p32#2/r11.anchor: دخل رجلان: رجل عقل عن الله تعالى وانتفع بما سمع، ورجل لم يعقل عن الله، فلم ينتفع بما سمع،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes identify the listeners as hypocrites at the Friday sermon; after the Prophet criticized them, they left the mosque and asked knowledgeable Companions what he had just said.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: يعني المنافقين يستمعون خطبة النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- يوم الجمعة، وكان يعرض بالمنافقين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas said, as transmitted by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he himself was among those whom the hypocrites questioned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r2.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: كنت فيمن سئل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس وابن بريدة ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r3.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas identifies the knowledgeable person as Abdullah ibn Masud; Ibn Burayda and Muqatil hold the same view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r3.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد عبد الله بن مسعود، وهو قول ابن بريدة (¬4) ومقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r4.claim: Abu Zayd explains آنفا as just now, deriving it from beginning or resuming speech; the root أنف denotes the first part of a thing, as with the first cold or rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r4.anchor: أي: ماذا قال الساعة، ويعني الآنف من الائتناف، وهو الابتداء يقال: ائتنفت الكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r5.claim: Imru al-Qays's phrase أنفه means the beginning of a horse's run, illustrating the sense of first or initial.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r5.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: قد غدا يحملني أنفه ... لاحق الأيطل محبوك ممر (¬1) أي: في أول جريه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r6.claim: Abu Ali says آنفا is formed from أنف although that verb is unattested; the pattern is possible because active participles can derive from otherwise unused verbs, as فقير and شديد do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r6.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: و (آنفا) من أنف، أي ابتدأ وهو غير مستعمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r7.claim: A report through al-Bazzi attributes to Ibn Kathir the form أنفا بالقمر, but al-Wahidi treats it as a mistaken supposition and upholds the common reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r7.anchor: وروى أحمد بن موسى بإسناده عن ابن كثير من طريق البزي: (أنفا) بالقمر (¬3)، وهذا يحمل على أنه توهمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r8.claim: The cited poem's أنف القصاع means the best and first portions of food, not leftovers; أنف is a plural form like قاتل and بازل.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r8.anchor: ويأكل جارهم أنف القصاع (¬4) يريد: أنهم يؤثرونه بأفضل الطعام وأوله لا البقايا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers that the hypocrites asked mockingly to show that they had not listened or paid attention; the alternative is that they heard but did not understand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r9.anchor: وهذا اختيار الزجاج (¬6)، القول الثاني: أنهم سمعوا كلامه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r1.claim: Muqatil and Ibn Abbas through Ikrima support the alternative that the hypocrites heard but did not understand; the context supports this reading, since they had no hearts attentive to the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: وقد سمعوا قول النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- فلم يفقهوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r2.claim: Muqatil says God sealed their hearts with disbelief so they could not understand faith, and they followed their desires in disbelief and hypocrisy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p240/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: ختم على قلوبهم بالكفر فلا يعقلون الإيمان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r2.claim: Those who listen to the Prophet and then ask what he said are hypocrites.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r2.anchor: ومنهم من يستمع إليك } يعني: المنافقين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r3.claim: They listened to the Prophet's sermon, then mockingly asked his Companions what he had just said, signaling that they had paid no attention.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:47:15-17/r3.anchor: كانوا يستمعون خطبة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وإذا خرجوا سألوا أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم استهزاء

ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r1.claim: Those who listen to the Prophet are hypocrites who attend his gathering but, lacking faith and care, fail to retain his words and treat them dismissively.
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r1.anchor: bunlar münafıklardır. Resûlullah’ın meclisine gelirler, kelâmını dinlerler, fakat iman ve itina ile dinlemedikleri için iyi bellemez, istihfaf ederlerdi.

ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r2.claim: After leaving, they ask the Companions who learned from the Prophet, “What did he just say?”
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r2.anchor: kendilerine ilim verilmiş olan, Resûlullah’ın kelâmından ders alıp da ilme nâil olan ashâb-ı kirâma “o demin ne dedi?” derlerdi.

ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r3.claim: One reported view says they asked this question of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r3.anchor: Bunu İbn Mes‘ûd Hazretleri’ne söylediklerine dair bir kavil vardır.

ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r4.claim: Their hearts are sealed because they follow only their own desires; consequently, the Prophet's words do not enter their ears or understanding.
ELMALILI:47:12-19#3/r4.anchor: kendilerinden ve kendi hevâlarından başka hiçbir şeye bakmayacak vechile kalbleri mühürlenmiş olduğundan dolayıdır ki kulaklarına söz girmez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r2.claim: Hypocrites stayed near the Prophet and listened, but without faith his words troubled them, so they resorted to mockery, irrelevant questions, and creating problems.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r2.anchor: Münafıklar Hz. Peygamber’in yanında ve yakınında bulunuyor ve onu dinliyorlardı, ama kalplerinde iman bulunmadığı için bu beraberlik ve ondan duydukları şeyler kendilerini rahatsız ediyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r3.claim: Asking others what the Prophet just said, despite having listened, both mocks what was heard and shows disregard for the speaker.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r3.anchor: Hem dinleyip hem de başkalarına “O şimdi ne dedi!” diye soru sormak, bir yandan dinlediklerini alaya almak, bir yandan da söyleyeni önemsememektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r4.claim: This conduct darkens the heart, conditions the mind, and blunts the ability to seek and recognize truth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:47:16/r4.anchor: Bu tavır ve davranışın sonu kalbin kararması, zihnin şartlanması, doğruyu arama ve bulma kabiliyetinin körleşmesidir.

QUSHAYRI:v3p201/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p201/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p201/r9.claim: The hypocrites disliked what God revealed because it exposed them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p201/r9.anchor: هم المنافقون الذين كرهوا ما أنزل الله ؛ لما فيه من افتضاحهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r1.claim: Al-samāʾ names anything above or elevated and derives from sumūw, elevation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r1.anchor: السماء في اللغة : اسم لكل ما علا وارتفع . وهو مأخوذ من السمو ، وهو العلو .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r2.claim: The source notes samā for sight rising or a figure becoming visible, and samāwa for the body of the moon.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r2.anchor: يقال : سما بصره ، أي : علا ، وسما لي شخص ، ارتفع حتى استثبته . وسماوة الهلال وكل شيء : شخصه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r3.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense is the familiar sky, as in its creation and provision above.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r3.anchor: أحدها : السماء المعروفة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r4.claim: Al-samāʾ can mean clouds, as in the passage about rainwater sent down and made drinkable.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r4.anchor: والثاني : السحاب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحجر : ^ ( فأنزلنا من السماء ماء ( فأسقيناكموه ) ^ )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r5.claim: A third sense is rain, as in Noah’s prayer that the sky be sent abundantly upon his people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r5.anchor: والثالث : المطر . ومنه قوله تعالى في نوح : ^ ( يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r6.claim: A fourth sense is a house roof, as in stretching a support up to the sky.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r6.anchor: والرابع : سقف البيت . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج : ^ ( فليمدد بسبب إلى السماء ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r7.claim: Al-samāʾ can mean the ceiling of Paradise or Hell, where inhabitants remain as long as heaven and earth endure.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p358#2/r7.anchor: والخامس : سقف الجنة وسقف النار . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود : ^ ( خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض ) ^

FARRA:v3p60/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p60/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p60/r1.claim: They listen to the Prophet's Friday sermon without understanding; after leaving with the people they mockingly ask the Muslims what he just said, and God describes their sealed hearts.
FARRA:v3p60/r1.anchor: ومنهم من يستمع إليك (16) . يعنى خطبتك فى الجمعة

MAJAZ:v2p215/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p215/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p215/r2.claim: Min here functions as a plural expression.
MAJAZ:v2p215/r2.anchor: «ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك» (16) من هاهنا فى موضع جميع..

NAHHAS:v4p184/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p184/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p184/r1.claim: Singular من has singular agreement first, then plural agreement by meaning in أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم واتبعوا أهواءهم.
NAHHAS:v4p184/r1.anchor: على لفظ من ( حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ) على المعنى

NAHHAS:v4p184/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p184/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
NAHHAS:v4p184/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Burayda says they asked this of ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd.
NAHHAS:v4p184/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله بن بريدة قالوا ذلك لعبد الله بن مسعود

SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses آنفا as a circumstantial accusative, expanded as ماذا قال مؤتنفا, meaning what he newly began to say.
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه منصوب على الحال، فقدره أبو البقاء: " ماذا قال مؤتنفا ".

SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r2.claim: Others also parse it as a circumstantial accusative meaning newly beginning: what did he start saying just before leaving?
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r2.anchor: وقدره غيره: مبتدئا أي: ما القول الذي ائتنفه الآن قبل انفصاله عنه.

SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses آنفا as an adverb meaning this very hour; Ibn ʿAtiyya instead explains it as the recent past, the near preceding moment.
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه منصوب على الظرف أي: ماذا قال الساعة، قاله الزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r4.claim: The Sheikh rejects the adverb parse, saying he knows no one who classifies آنفا as an adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r4.anchor: وأنكره الشيخ قال: " لأنا لم نعلم أحدا عده من الظروف ".

SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r5.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives آنفا from استأنفت الشيء, to begin something, glossing it as what he said at the beginning of the time close to us.
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: " هو من استأنفت الشيء إذا ابتدأته أي: ماذا قال في أول وقت يقرب منا ".

SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r6.speaker: البزي
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r6.claim: Al-Bazzi has a variant shortening the alif in أنفا; the others lengthen it. Both are synonymous active participles, from verbs used only in derived forms for beginning.
SAMIN-DURR:47:16/r6.anchor: وقرأ البزي بخلاف عنه " أنفا " بالقصر. والباقون بالمد، وهما لغتان بمعنى واحد،

ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r2.claim: Those who listen to the Prophet and then ask what he said are hypocrites.
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r2.anchor: يعني المنافقين. (حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك

ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r3.claim: They listened to the Prophet's sermon, then asked the Companions what he had just said in mockery and to show they had paid no attention.
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r3.anchor: كانوا يسمعون خطبة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فإذا خرجوا سألوا أصحاب رسول الله

ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r4.claim: Ānifan means just now or at the near beginning; the word relates to beginning something anew and to a pasture not yet grazed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p10/r4.anchor: أي ماذا قال الساعة، ومعنى آنفا من قولك استأنفت الشيء إذا ابتدأته

ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n18/r1.claim: Asad points to 6:25 and 10:42–43 for related instances of people listening without understanding.

ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r1.claim: “Those who have been given knowledge” means believers who know the truth or Muhammad's message.
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r1.anchor: "of the truth" or "of thy message": i.e., the believers.

ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r2.claim: The listeners are hypocrites among Muhammad's contemporaries and, more broadly, people who feign reverence for the Qur'an while inwardly refusing to admit meaning in it.
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n19/r2.anchor: who pretend to approach the Qur'anic message with a show of "reverence" but are in their innermost unwilling to admit that there is any sense in it.

ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n20/r1.claim: The sealing of these listeners' hearts results from their following their own desires.
ASAD-NOTES:47:16#n20/r1.anchor: is a consequence of their "following but their own lusts".

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir is reported by al-Bazzi with the short form آنفا, though Qunbul also reports the long form; all other readers use the long form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحده: ماذا قال آنفا [محمد/ 16] قصرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r2.claim: Abu Zayd explains ائتنفت الكلام as beginning speech anew, the sense intended by the verse's آنفا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r2.anchor: قال أبو زيد: ائتنفت الكلام ائتنافا وابتدأته ابتداء وهما واحد.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r3.speaker: السكري
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r3.claim: Al-Sukkari says الأنف in poetry means people who refuse humiliation; al-Farisi says those examples do not bear the verse's sense of beginning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r3.anchor: قال السكري: الأنف الذين يأنفون من احتمال الضيم، فقال أبو علي: فإذا كان كذا

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r4.claim: Abu Zayd's verse calls the subjects الأنف الكرام, poetic evidence for proud, unyielding people rather than beginning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r4.anchor: وأنشد أبو زيد: وجدنا آل مرة حين خفنا جريرتنا هم الأنف الكراما

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r5.claim: A poem uses الأنف as a resolute adjective; a Sibawayh line about نمر illustrates a parallel broken plural pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r5.anchor: وحمال المئين إذا ألمت بنا الحدثان والأنف النصور

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r6.claim: The poem جارهم أنف القصاع means they give guests the best, freshest food first, supporting the sense of beginning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r6.anchor: ويأكل جارهم أنف القصاع فإنه يريد: أنهم يؤثرون ضيفهم بأفضل الطعام وجيده،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r7.claim: The long reading is preferable because the Quran means newly begun, from ائتنف; the short report may analogize the word to حاذر/حذر.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r7.anchor: وما في الآية: من الابتداء ولم يسمع أنف في معنى ابتداء، وإن كان القياس يوجبه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies those who listen to the Prophet without understanding as hypocrites.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ومنهم من يستمع إليك ﴾ قال هم المنافقون

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r2.claim: Qatāda transmits a saying that listeners are of three kinds: one hears and acts, one hears and understands, and one hears but abandons it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p222#5/r2.anchor: قال وكان يقال الناس ثلاثة سامع فعامل وسامع فعاقل وسامع فتارك

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r1.claim: The listeners are hypocrites; the singular in يستمع follows the word's grammatical form, while the later plural follows its meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r1.anchor: هم المنافقون وإفراد الضمير باعتبار اللفظ كما أن جمعه بعد باعتبار المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they attended the Messenger's gathering and heard him but paid no heed or proper attention out of disdain.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج : كانوا يحضرون مجلس رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فيسمعون كلامه

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r3.claim: Those given knowledge are the learned Companions; alternatively, they are the Companions who attended to the Prophet's speech with due care.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r3.anchor: أي لأولي العلم من الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r4.claim: The question usually feigns inquiry to mock the Prophet; it may instead be a genuine question from inattention, which is why they are still condemned, but the mocking reading is preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r4.anchor: ومقصودهم من ذك الأستهزاء وإن كان بصورة الأستعلام وجوز أن يكون مرادهم حقيقة الأستعلام

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says he himself is among those given knowledge and named among those asked about the Prophet's words.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنا منهم وقد سميت فيمن سئل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r6.claim: Anifan is a non-regular active participle, or one formed after removing the derived prefix, since only istaʾnafa and atʾanafa are attested verbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r6.anchor: لم يسمع له فعل ثلاثي بل استأنف وأتنف

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives anifan from istaʾnaft al-shayʾ, to begin something: its original image is taking its nose or beginning, then nose came to mean a thing's front or foremost part.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r7.anchor: وذكر الزجاج أنه من استأنفت الشيء إذا ابتدأته وكان أصل معنى هذا أخذت أنفه

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r8.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r8.claim: Several authorities explain anifan as the time just before the present, by metaphor from the nose's forward position; another view makes it the present moment.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r8.anchor: وذكر غير واحد أن آنفا من ذلك قالوا : إنه للساعة التي قبل ساعتك التي أنت فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats anifan as an adverb of time, which is compatible with its participial form because such forms can be lexicalized as adverbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r9.anchor: وهو على ما ذهب إليه الزمخشري نصب على الظرفية ولا ينافي كونه اسم فاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan says it is not an adverb, since grammarians do not classify it as one; it is a circumstantial accusative of the speaker, meaning what he had just begun saying before they left.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الصحيح أنه ليس بظرف ولا نعلم أحدا من النحاة عده

ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir reads anifan on the faʿl pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p50#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ( آنفا على وزن فعل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p51/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p51/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p51/r1.claim: They turned toward everything devoid of good, which explains their conduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p51/r1.anchor: فتوجهوا نحو كل ما لا خير فيه فلذلك كان منهم ما كان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r1.claim: Those who listen to Muḥammad are hypocrites who do not understand or heed him, out of disdain and deliberate inattention.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r1.anchor: وهم المنافقون، يستمعون قولك فلا يعونه ولا يفهمونه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r2.claim: The phrase means 'when they leave your presence.'

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r3.claim: The people of knowledge they question are Companions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r3.anchor: قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم} من الصحابة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r4.claim: Ānifan means 'just now'; it derives from beginning or resuming something, and anaf is a thing's beginning.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r5.claim: Muqātil says the Prophet criticized the hypocrites in his sermon, and on leaving the mosque they mockingly asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd what he had said.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخطب ويعيب المنافقين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he too was among those asked.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وقد سئلت فيمن سئل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#3/r1.claim: God sealed their hearts so that they did not believe.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#3/r1.anchor: {أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم} فلم يؤمنوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p283#3/r2.claim: They followed their desires in disbelief and hypocrisy.

BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.claim: The listeners are hypocrites who attended the Messenger's gathering and heard him speak.
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.anchor: يعني المنافقين كانوا يحضرون مجلس الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ويسمعون كلامه

BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.claim: Those given knowledge are the learned Companions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.anchor: أي لعلماء الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.claim: Their question may be mocking; alternatively, they ask what the Messenger just said because they did not listen attentively out of disregard.
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.anchor: ما الذي قال الساعة، استهزاء أو استعلاما إذا لم يلقوا له آذانهم تهاونا به

BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.claim: Ānifan means just now, derived from the front of a thing and borrowed from the nose; the related verbs mean to begin anew.
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.anchor: من قولهم أنف الشيء لما تقدم منه مستعار من الجارحة، ومنه استأنف وائتنف

BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.claim: Ānifan functions either as an adverb meaning a newly begun time or as a circumstantial expression attached to the pronoun in he said.
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.anchor: وهو ظرف بمعنى وقتا مؤتنفا، أو حال من الضمير في { قال }

BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the word as anfa.

BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:47:16-17/r7.claim: God sealed their hearts and they followed their desires, which is why they mocked and disregarded the Messenger's speech.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r1.claim: Some listen with great effort hoping to find a flaw in the recitation with which to sow doubt among the weak.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r1.anchor: { ومنهم من يستمع } أي بغاية جهده لعله يجد في المتلو مطعنا يشك به على الضعفاء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r2.claim: The singular listener follows the grammar of من and signals the few who listen; the shift to plural follows its meaning and signals the many who turn away or mock.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r2.anchor: ولما أفرد المستمع نظرا إلى لفظ ( من ) إشارةإلى قلة المستمع جمع نظرا إلى معناه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r3.claim: Both the hostile listeners and others who heard the sermon ask the question after leaving, doing so in blindness, feigned ignorance, and mockery.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r3.anchor: { إذا خرجوا } أي المستمعون والسامعون جميعا { من عندك قالوا } أي الفريقان عمى وتعاميا واستهزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r4.claim: The passive wording magnifies beneficial knowledge; God prepared its recipients with clear minds free of ego and responsive to primordial nature.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r4.anchor: { للذين أوتوا العلم } أي بسبب تهيئة الله لهم بما آتاهم من صفاء الأفهام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r5.claim: آنفا means just now, shortly before they left; its sense is linked to the first or foremost part, as with the beginning of prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r5.anchor: { آنفا } أي قبل افتراقنا وخروجنا عنه من ساعة - أي أول وقت - تقرب منه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan construes آنفا as a circumstantial accusative meaning beginning or newly initiated, asking what the Prophet had just begun to say before they separated.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r6.anchor: قال أبو حيان : حال , اي مبتدئا , أي ما القول الذي ائتنفه الآن قبل انفصالنا عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r7.claim: The author rejects treating آنفا as an adverb: the explanation gives its sense, and he knows no grammarian who classifies it as an adverb.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r7.anchor: ورد كونه ظرفا بأنه تفسير معنى , وأنه لا يعلم أحدا من النحاة عده في الظروف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r8.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r8.claim: Al-Baghawi says ائتنفت الأمر means I began the matter, while أنف الشيء is its beginning.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r8.anchor: وقال البغوي : ائتنفت الأمر : ابتدأته , وأنف الشيء أوله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r9.speaker: مقاتل
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r9.claim: Muqatil's account says the Prophet preached and censured hypocrites, who mockingly asked Ibn Masud what Muhammad had said as they left the mosque.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r9.anchor: قال مقاتل : وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخطب ويعيب المنافقين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says that he was among those who were asked.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : وقد سئلت فيمن سئل .

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r11.claim: God sealed their hearts so that they neither believed nor understood for benefit; such rigid indifference results from that seal.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r11.anchor: فلم يؤمنوا ولم يفهموا فهم الانتفاع لأن مثل هذا الجمود لا يكون إلا بذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r12.claim: By following their desires they abandoned reason and human restraint, neglected the greatest discourse, and pursued worldly accumulation; they are the people of Hell described before the Garden parable.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p162/r12.anchor: أي مجانبين لوازع العقل وناهي المروءة , فلذلك هم يتهاونون بأعظم الكلام ويقبلون على جمع الحطام

DURR-FULL:v7p465/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says believers heard and retained the Prophet's words, while hypocrites heard without understanding; on leaving, they asked what he had just said, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه قال: كان المؤمنون والمنافقون يجتمعون إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p465/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says visitors leaving the Prophet asked Ibn ʿAbbās what he had just said; Ibn ʿAbbās would tell them, and was among those given knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: كانوا يدخلون على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإذا خرجوا من عنده قالوا لابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ماذا قال آنفا

DURR-FULL:v7p465/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that he himself was one of those endowed with knowledge and had been asked what the Prophet had just said.
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا} قال: أنا منهم ولقد سئلت

DURR-FULL:v7p465/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r6.claim: Qatāda distinguishes two listeners: one understood God's message and benefited, while the other neither understood nor retained nor benefited from it.
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {ومنهم من يستمع إليك} قال: هؤلاء المنافقون دخل رجلان فرجل عقل عن الله وانتفع بما يسمع

DURR-FULL:v7p465/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r7.speaker: ابن بريدة
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r7.claim: Ibn Burayda identifies the people endowed with knowledge as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r7.anchor: عن ابن بريدة رضي الله عنه {قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا} قال: هو عبد الله بن مسعود

DURR-FULL:v7p465/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r8.claim: A report through al-Kalbī and Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās also identifies the learned listener as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
DURR-FULL:v7p465/r8.anchor: عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: هو عبد الله بن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r1.claim: Some attend the Prophet and listen to his speech and recitation, then on leaving ask willing believers what he had just said.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r1.anchor: يحضرون عند النبي عليه السلام فيسمعون كلامه وتلاوته، فإذا خرجوا قال بعضهم لمن شاء من المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r2.claim: Some ask in mockery, meaning what did his words mean, benefit, or amount to?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r2.anchor: فكان منهم من يقول هذا استخفافا، أي ما معنى ما قال وما نفعه وما قدره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r3.claim: Others ask out of ignorance or forgetfulness because they were absorbed in worldly thoughts and unbelief; this too shows contempt by openly admitting they ignored the speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r3.anchor: ومنهم من كان يقول ذلك جهالة ونسيانا، لأنه كان في وقت الكلام مقبلا على فكرته في أمر دنياه وفي كفره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas were among those asked this question; al-Tabari transmits the report from Ibn ʿAbbas.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r4.anchor: وروي أن عبد الله بن مسعود وابن عباس ممن سئل هذا السؤال، حكاه الطبري عن ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r5.claim: Most readers read آنفا on the pattern fāʿil.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir alone reads أنفا on the pattern faʿl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحده: «أنفا» على وزن فعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r7.claim: Both forms are active participles from ائتنف used without their corresponding verb, as فقير derives from افتقر without فقَر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r7.anchor: وهما اسما فاعل من ائتنف، وجريا على غير فعلهما، وهذا كما جرى فقير على افتقر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r8.claim: Commentators explain the word by its sense: the recent moment just past.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r8.anchor: والمفسرون يقولون: «أنفا» معناه: الساعة الماضية القريبة منا، وهذا تفسير بالمعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r9.claim: The sealing of these hypocrites’ hearts may be literal or metaphorical; Ibn ʿAṭiyya refers back to his earlier discussion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p115/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أنه طبع على قلوب هؤلاء المنافقين الفاعلين لهذا، وهذا الطبع يحتمل أن يكون حقيقة، ويحتمل أن يكون استعارة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r1.claim: The people described as listening are the hypocrites.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r2.claim: One view says they listen to the Prophet's Friday sermon.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه سماع خطبة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الجمعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r3.claim: A second view takes the listening to refer generally to what the Prophet says at any time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r3.anchor: والثاني سماع قوله على عموم الأوقات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r4.claim: Those given knowledge are the learned Companions.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says anifan means “just now,” deriving it from beginning something anew and from a pasture not yet grazed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج أي ماذا قال الساعة وهو من قولك استأنفت الشيء إذا ابتدأته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r6.speaker: أبو عمر غلام ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r6.claim: Abu Umar, Thalab's servant, glosses anifan as “a little while ago.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r6.anchor: وحدثنا عن أبي عمر غلام ثعلب أنه قال معنى آنفا مذ ساعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وعكرمة وحميد وابن محيصن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r7.claim: In some transmissions Ibn Kathir, as well as Ikrima, Humayd, and Ibn Muhaysin, reads anifan without lengthening.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير في بعض الروايات عنه أنفا بالقصر وهذه قراءة عكرمة وحميد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r8.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r8.claim: Abu ʿAli suggests Ibn Kathir may have confused the form with pairs such as ḥādhir and ḥadhir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي يجوز أن يكون ابن كثير توهم مثل حاذر وحذر وفاكه وفكه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r9.claim: Their question may be because they did not understand what was said, as the verse's continuation indicates, or because they meant to mock.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p402/r9.anchor: وفي استفهامهم قولان أحدهما لأنهم لم يعقلوا ما يقول ويدل عليه باقي الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r1.claim: The hypocrites sit with the Prophet and hear him without understanding; after leaving, they ask the knowledgeable Companions what he said.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r1.anchor: حيث كانوا يجلسون إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويستمعون كلامه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r2.claim: آنفا means “just now” or “a moment ago.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r2.anchor: قال آنفا} أي: الساعة، لا يعقلون ما يقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r3.claim: God’s sealing leaves them without sound understanding or a sound intention, and they follow their desires.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p315/r3.anchor: أي: فلا فهم صحيح، ولا قصد صحيح

JISHUMI:v9p6447/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6447/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6447/r9.claim: One report says the phrase was revealed about Abū Jahl and his associates among the polytheists.
JISHUMI:v9p6447/r9.anchor: وقيل: نزل قوله: (واتبعوا أهواءهم) في أبي جهل وأصحابه من المشركين

JISHUMI:v9p6447/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6447/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6447/r23.claim: Following desires applies generally to every unbeliever and innovator; limiting it to Abū Jahl and his associates is not the sound view because wording is generalized beyond its occasion.
JISHUMI:v9p6447/r23.anchor: واتبعوا أهواءهم عام في كل كافر ومبتدع، وقيل: أبو جهل وأصحابه، وليس بالوجه؛ لأن المراعي عموم اللفظ لا السبب

JISHUMI:v9p6450/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r5.claim: In one transmission, Ibn Kathīr reads anfan without lengthening the initial vowel.
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير في إحدى الروايتين عنه: أنفا بغير مد

JISHUMI:v9p6450/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r6.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r6.claim: The other readers lengthen the initial vowel, reading ānifan.

JISHUMI:v9p6450/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r7.claim: Ānif means just now or the beginning of a discourse; its root is istānafa, to begin, and related uses include fresh pasture, a newly used cup, a thing's beginning, and the start of a run.
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r7.anchor: الآنف: الجائي بأول المعنى، مأخوذ من استأنفت الشيء: ابتدأته

JISHUMI:v9p6450/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r8.claim: Ṭabʿ and khatm are synonymous: a mark placed on something.
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r8.anchor: والطبع والختم بمعنى، وهو علامة تجعل على الشيء

JISHUMI:v9p6450/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r9.claim: Hawā is the soul's desire and inclination; al-hawā with a long vowel means air, and istahwā means to call someone toward desire.
JISHUMI:v9p6450/r9.anchor: والهوى: هوى النفس، وهو ميله إليها، والهواء بالمد الجو، استهواه الأمر، أي: دعاه إلى الهوى

JISHUMI:v9p6451/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r5.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r5.claim: The passage concerns hypocrites who, after the Prophet preached and criticized them, asked Ibn Masʿūd what he had said when they left.
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r5.anchor: عن مقاتل. وقال ابن عباس: (للذين أوتوا) أنا منهم، وقد سئلت فيمن سئل

JISHUMI:v9p6451/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r6.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r6.claim: Moqātil identifies those given knowledge as Ibn Masʿūd, whom the departing hypocrites asked what the Prophet had said.
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r6.anchor: (للذين أوتوا العلم) في ابن مسعود، وذلك أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان يخطب الناس

JISHUMI:v9p6451/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he himself was among those given knowledge and had been asked along with the others.
JISHUMI:v9p6451/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: (للذين أوتوا) أنا منهم، وقد سئلت فيمن سئل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r1.claim: They are hypocrites who attend the Prophet's gathering but heed nothing out of disdain, then mockingly ask the knowledgeable Companions what he just said.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r1.anchor: كانوا يحضرون مجلس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r2.claim: One account says that when the Prophet criticized hypocrites while preaching, they left and asked the scholars what he said.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r2.anchor: كان يخطب فإذا عاب المنافقين خرجوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r3.claim: Another account identifies Abdullah ibn Masud as the person they asked.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r3.anchor: وقيل : قالوه لعبد الله بن مسعود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas said he was among those addressed and had been named among those questioned.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r4.anchor: أنا منهم ، وقد سميت فيمن سئل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r5.claim: A variant reads أنفا on the pattern فعل, in the adverbial accusative.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r6.speaker: الزجاج
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives it from استأنفت الشيء, meaning that I began something.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r6.anchor: هو من استأنفت الشيء : إذا ابتدأته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r7.claim: The question means what he said at the first moment close to them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p325/r7.anchor: ماذا قال في أول وقت يقرب منا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r1.claim: Mawardi identifies the listeners as hypocrites: Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Rifa'a ibn al-Tabut, Zayd ibn al-Sulayt, al-Harith ibn Amr, and Malik ibn al-Dakhsham.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r1.anchor: هم المنافقون : عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول , ورفاعة بن التابوت ، وزيد بن الصليت , والحارث بن عمرو ، ومالك بن الدخشم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say they attended Friday sermons, ignored mention of hypocrites, then asked what was said after leaving.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم كانوا يحضرون الخطبة يوم الجمعة فإذا سمعوا ذكر المنافقين فيها أعرضوا عنه ، فإذا خرجوا سألوا عنه , قاله الكلبي ومقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r3.claim: Another explanation is that hypocrites sat with believers before the Prophet: believers understood his words, but hypocrites did not.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنهم كانوا يحضرون عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع المؤمنين , فيسمعون منه ما يقول , فيعيه المؤمن ولا يعيه المنافق .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r4.claim: “From your presence” means from the presence of the Messenger of God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r4.anchor: حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك } أي من عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r5.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r5.claim: Ikrima identifies those given knowledge as Ibn Abbas.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r5.anchor: أحدها : أنه عبد الله بن عباس ، قاله عكرمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r6.claim: Abd Allah ibn Burayda identifies those given knowledge as Ibn Masud.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r6.anchor: الثاني : عبد الله بن مسعود , قاله عبد الله بن بريدة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r7.speaker: القاسم بن عبد الرحمن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r7.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman identifies the knowledgeable person as Abu al-Darda.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r7.anchor: الثالث : أبو الدرداء , قاله القاسم بن عبد الرحمن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd takes those given knowledge to mean the Companions collectively.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r8.anchor: الرابع : أنهم الصحابة , قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r9.claim: This is the hypocrites' question to the knowledgeable people after leaving the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r9.anchor: هذا سؤال المنافقين للذين أوتوا العلم إذا خرجوا من عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r10.claim: Anif can mean recently or at the beginning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r10.anchor: وفيه وجهان : أحدهما : يعني قريبا . الثاني : مبتدئا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r11.claim: Their question may mock what they heard or seek information about what they failed to understand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r11.anchor: وفي مقصودهم بهذا السؤال وجهان : أحدهما : الإستهزاء بما سمعوه . الثاني : البحث عما جهلوه .

MUQATIL:47:16/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:47:16/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:47:16/r1.claim: The people listening to Muhammad here are hypocrites.
MUQATIL:47:16/r1.anchor: { ومنهم } يعني من المنافقين { من يستمع إليك } يعني إلى حديثك بالقرآن

MUQATIL:47:16/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:47:16/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:47:16/r2.claim: Among the listeners were Rifaah ibn Zayd, al-Harith ibn Amr, and an ally of Banu Zuhra; after Muhammad criticized hypocrites in his Friday sermon, they kept quiet and left.
MUQATIL:47:16/r2.anchor: منهم رفاعة بن زيد، والحارث بن عمرو، وحليف بني زهرة، وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خطب يوم الجمعة

MUQATIL:47:16/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:47:16/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:47:16/r3.claim: Those given knowledge are guided by the Quran; Muqatil identifies them here as Abdullah ibn Masud al-Hudhali.
MUQATIL:47:16/r3.anchor: { قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم } وهو الهدى، يعني القرآن، يعني عبدالله بن مسعود الهذلي

MUQATIL:47:16/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:47:16/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:47:16/r4.claim: The hypocrites ask what Muhammad just said despite having heard him, because they did not understand his words.
MUQATIL:47:16/r4.anchor: { ماذا قال } محمد { آنفا } وقد سمعوا قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يفقهوه

MUQATIL:47:16/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:47:16/r5.speaker: author
