MUQATIL:47:16/r5.claim: God sealed their hearts with disbelief so they cannot understand faith, and they follow their desires in disbelief.
MUQATIL:47:16/r5.anchor: يعني ختم الله على قلوبهم بالكفر فلا يعقلون الإيمان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r1.claim: These are hypocrites who attend the Prophet's gathering, hear without understanding or paying attention out of disdain, then ask the knowledgeable Companions what he said just now mockingly.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r1.anchor: كانوا يحضرون مجلس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيسمعون كلامه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r2.claim: Ānifan means “just now” or “at this moment.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p148/r2.anchor: قالوا لاولى العلم من الصحابة ماذا قال الساعة على جهة الاستهزاء

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil identify the listeners as hypocrites, including ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, Rifāʿa ibn al-Tābūt, Zayd ibn al-Ṣalt, al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr, and Mālik ibn Dukhshum; they attended Friday sermons, ignored mention of hypocrites, then asked about it afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r1.anchor: كانوا يحضرون الخطبة يوم الجمعة فإذا سمعوا ذكر المنافقين فيها أعرضوا عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.claim: Another view says they listened to the Prophet among the believers, but believers retained and understood his words while unbelievers did not.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r2.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يحضرون عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع المؤمنين فيستمعون منه ما يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.claim: The phrase means when they left or parted from the Prophet’s gathering.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r3.anchor: حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك } أي إذا فارقوا مجلسك

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.claim: ʿIkrima identifies those given knowledge as ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās; Ibn ʿAbbās says he was among those questioned and thus among the learned.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r4.anchor: قال عكرمة: هو عبد الله بن العباس. قال ابن عباس: كنت ممن يسأل

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، عبد الله بن بريدة
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.claim: Another transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda identifies the learned person as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r5.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس: أنه يريد عبد الله بن مسعود. وكذا قال عبد الله بن بريدة

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r6.speaker: القاسم بن عبد الرحمن، ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r6.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān identifies the learned person as Abū al-Dardāʾ; Ibn Zayd says the phrase refers to the Companions collectively.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r6.anchor: وقال القاسم بن عبد الرحمن: هو أبو الدرداء. وقال ابن زيد: إنهم الصحابة

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r7.claim: They ask “what did he just say?” mockingly, as though they had paid no attention; ānifan denotes the time nearest to the present, from beginning something anew.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r7.anchor: ماذا قال آنفا } أي الآن على جهة الاستهزاء. أي أنا لم ألتفت إلى قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r8.claim: Anf can mean the beginning: fresh pasture or an unused cup; anonymous poems illustrate that sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r8.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
ويحرم سر جارتهم عليهم
ويأكل جارهم أنف القصاع

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r9.claim: A second poem uses anf for an unused cup; Imruʾ al-Qays uses the term for the beginning of a journey, and the nose of anything is its beginning.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r9.anchor: وقال آخر: إن الشواء والنشيل والرغف والقينة الحسناء والكأس الأنف

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r10.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r10.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses anf for the beginning, as in “he carried me in his beginning.”
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r10.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: قد غدا يحملني في أنفه أي في أوله

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r11.claim: Qatāda contrasts someone who understands God’s message and benefits from hearing it with someone who neither understands nor benefits; another saying divides listeners into acting, understanding, and heedlessly abandoning hearers.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة في هؤلاء المنافقين: الناس رجلان: رجل عقل عن الله فانتفع بما سمع

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r12.claim: God sealed their hearts, so they did not believe.
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r12.anchor: { أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم } فلم يؤمنوا

QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:47:16-17/r13.claim: They followed their desires in disbelief.
